factProposals.value: The dead-letter queue is a second Redis Stream (relay:jobs:dlq in production usage), read/written through the same RedisStreamQueue class as the primary job queue.
A circuit-open rejection (CircuitOpenError) is explicitly NOT treated as retries-exhausted and does not move a job to the DLQ - only UpstreamCallFailedError does.
DLQ triage is currently a manual, code-level action (no CLI or UI yet) - a human runs triageNextDeadLetterEntry() directly per docs/runbooks/DLQ_TRIAGE.md.

decisions.statement: The DLQ reuses RedisStreamQueue (the same class STORY-002 built for the primary queue) rather than a new queue mechanism.
decisions.rationale: a dead-letter queue is structurally just another durable stream a job lands in instead of vanishing; building a second mechanism would duplicate logic already proven correct.

decisions.statement: The original job's payload is preserved whole inside the DLQ entry (payload.originalPayload), alongside the failure reason and timestamp, rather than discarding or reshaping it.
decisions.rationale: triage needs the real job to decide whether resubmission is safe; a DLQ entry that lost the original data would be undebuggable.

limitations.statement: No automated retry-from-DLQ exists - resubmission after triage is a manual action described in the runbook, not code.
No DLQ size or age alerting exists - nothing pages anyone when the DLQ grows or an entry sits untriaged.
